sentences.text: Weewarrasaurus is classified as a genus of ornithopod dinosaur within the suborder Neornithischia and the infraorder Ornithopoda of the order Ornithischia.
It remains the only known species in the extinct elasmarian ornithopod genus.
The holotype fossil is notable for being preserved in green-blue opal.
Natural opal banding patterns allowed researchers to confirm that the two broken jaw sections belonged to the same individual.
The type specimen was first discovered in 2013 by miners, and paleontologist Phil Bell examined the specimen in 2014 to recognize its scientific importance.

The genus name Weewarrasaurus combines the Wee Warra fossil locality with the Greek word saurus, meaning lizard, while the species name W. pobeni honors Mike Poben, the opal dealer who first identified the fossil.
A second partial jawbone, specimen LRF 766, was referred to the species based on similar tooth morphology.
Weewarrasaurus likely co-existed with various other ornithopods of different sizes and evolutionary lineages.
Weewarrasaurus lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 100 to 93 million years ago, with the fossil record spanning from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
Fossils of Weewarrasaurus have been found in the Griman Creek Formation near Lightning Ridge, New South Wales, Australia.
